newsitem.title: UK: BA jet tried to land at wrong end of runway.
newsitem.headline: BA jet tried to land at wrong end of runway.

text.p: A British Airways jet with 166 people on board tried to land in the wrong direction at London's Gatwick airport after the co-pilot took sleep-inducing pills and collapsed, leaving the pilot to fly by himself, investigators said on Thursday.

The Air Accident Investigations Branch (AAIB) said the commander of the Boeing B-767 airliner mistakenly thought he was supposed to be landing at Gatwick's sole runway from the left although controllers had mentioned three times that planes should land from the right.

The plane, which was en route from Pittsburgh, was forced to abort its approach to give the pilot time to re-programme the on-board computers and land safely. The incident took place in December last year.
No comment was immediately available from British Airways on the pilot's error.
The AAIB told BA to make sure its pilots were aware of what medication they could safely take when on duty after the co-pilot took what he thought were paracetamol-type painkillers.

But the pills contained a mixture of paracetamol and codeine phosphate -- which British authorities consider to be incompatible with flying duties -- and he collapsed in one of the plane's lavatories.
